title: Proxima Fusion
summary: Munich company designing a stellarator fusion power plant based on Wendelstein 7-X research.
bodyHtml:
Proxima Fusion is a spin-out of the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics, working on a stellarator design that uses complex twisted magnetic coils to confine plasma steadily.

Stellarators are harder to build than tokamaks but are intrinsically more stable, which matters for continuous power production.

Why it matters

  • Stellarator power-plant design
  • High-temperature superconducting magnets
  • Public research heritage

businessMeaning: Fusion timelines are long, and the stellarator route bets on steady-state operation over tokamak experience. Magnet manufacturing is the near-term bottleneck.
investmentLens: Private; the public read is superconducting tape and precision magnet suppliers.
